subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change gateway-host exec private-LAN reachability semantics?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current generic error surface, but allowing or intentionally blocking private-LAN exec traffic is a security-boundary and product-policy choice that needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR after required checks are refreshed, while leaving private-LAN access semantics unchanged and tracked separately.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent reachability as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Policy Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only mitigation and keep this behavior under the broader private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR after required checks are refreshed, while leaving private-LAN access semantics unchanged and tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The exec runtime history and the security/product scope most consistently route through this exec surface owner signal.
